title: Modes of connection
starter: Count the devices around you that connect without a cable. For each one, say why a cable would be worse.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: Ethernet
facts: A wired standard for connecting devices on a LAN.
Data is sent in frames containing source and destination addresses.
Uses twisted pair or fibre optic cable, usually into a switch.
stations.challenge: Why do many gamers plug their console into the router with a cable?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A wired standard for connecting devices on a LAN.
Also credit: Data is sent in frames containing source and destination addresses.

questions.q: What type of connection is Ethernet?
What does an Ethernet frame contain so it reaches the right device?

stations.name: Wi-Fi
facts: A wireless connection using radio waves, through a wireless access point.
Range of around 100 metres, less indoors.
High bandwidth, but uses more power than Bluetooth.
stations.challenge: What does a laptop need to connect to Wi-Fi?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A wireless connection using radio waves, through a wireless access point.
Also credit: Range of around 100 metres, less indoors.

questions.q: What is the typical range of Wi-Fi?
What does a device need in order to join a Wi-Fi network?
questions.a: A wireless NIC, and to be in range of a wireless access point

stations.name: Bluetooth
facts: A short-range wireless connection directly between two devices.
Low bandwidth and low power consumption.
stations.challenge: Why is Bluetooth better than Wi-Fi for wireless earbuds?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A short-range wireless connection directly between two devices.
Also credit: Range of around 10 metres.

questions.q: What is the typical range of Bluetooth?
Why is Bluetooth good for wireless earbuds?
questions.a: It uses very little power, so batteries last longer

stations.name: Wi-Fi vs Bluetooth
facts: Complete the table on your worksheet for range, bandwidth and power consumption.
stations.challenge: Which would you use to transfer a 2 GB video from a laptop to a school server, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Complete the table on your worksheet for range, bandwidth and power consumption.

questions.q: Does each feature describe Wi-Fi or Bluetooth?
questions.a: Range of about 100 metres = Wi-Fi; Range of about 10 metres = Bluetooth; High bandwidth = Wi-Fi; Low bandwidth = Bluetooth; Higher power consumption = Wi-Fi; Low power consumption = Bluetooth

stations.name: Wired vs wireless
facts: Wired: faster, more reliable and easier to secure, but needs lots of cabling.
Wireless: access from anywhere in range and less disruptive to set up, but slower, less secure, and blocked by walls.
stations.challenge: Which is better: a wired or a wireless network? Give both sides.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Wired: faster, more reliable and easier to secure, but needs lots of cabling.
Also credit: Wireless: access from anywhere in range and less disruptive to set up, but slower, less secure, and blocked by walls.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a wired connection over wireless?
questions.a: It is usually faster and more reliable

questions.q: Why is a wireless network usually harder to secure?
questions.a: Its signals travel through the air, so anyone in range could try to connect or intercept them

stations.name: Recommend a connection
facts: Think about speed, reliability, security, range, power use and how easy it is to set up.
Always justify your choice with the scenario.
stations.challenge: Recommend a connection for a café offering free internet to customers. Justify your choice.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Think about speed, reliability, security, range, power use and how easy it is to set up.
Also credit: Always justify your choice with the scenario.

questions.q: A school hall needs 30 laptops online for one day. Which connection is best?
A server room needs the fastest, most reliable links. Which connection is best?
A wireless mouse for a laptop: which connection is best?

final.name: Final challenge: wired or wireless?

questions.q: Does each statement describe wired or wireless connections?
questions.a: Thick walls and other signals can interrupt it = Wireless; Needs cable runs, sockets and switches everywhere = Wired; Speeds drop the further you are from the access point = Wireless; A cable gives the same speed every time = Wired; An attacker has to get inside the building to tap it = Wired; Signals spread outside the building where anyone can capture them = Wireless; Best choice for machines that never move = Wired; Lets a class of laptops move room to room = Wireless; Can be set up in an old building without drilling holes = Wireless; Handles very large file transfers most quickly = Wired; Performance drops as more devices join the same access point = Wireless

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: Describe two differences between Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
points: High bandwidth, but uses more power than Bluetooth.
A short-range wireless connection directly between two devices.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 4.

exam.q: Explain one benefit and one drawback of using cables rather than Wi-Fi.
points: A wireless connection using radio waves, through a wireless access point.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 4.

points: A wireless connection using radio waves, through a wireless access point.
Always justify your choice with the scenario.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
